side-to-side-blend.motion: Start with Warm gold around where the sun will go and stroke side to side out from it. Without rinsing, pick up Misty blue-gray and paint it beyond the gold, toward the edges. Then stroke back over the join several times.
side-to-side-blend.result: A soft gold glow fading into misty gray-blue, with a soft join where the two wet colors meet.
side-to-side-blend.then: Stroke back over the join between the gold and the gray while it's wet.

mistakes.mistake: A hard line where the gold meets the gray.
mistakes.fix: Add more Warm gold at the join and blend again.

mistakes.mistake: The gold and the gray won't blend and turn muddy.
mistakes.fix: Mix a bridge color from the two on the palette and paint it between them.
Wipe it on a rag. Rinse before going into the gray.

diagram.title: Blend the gold glow into the gray

stages.caption: Gold around the sun, side to side

small-circles.motion: Small circles with the tip of the brush, starting at the sun's center and moving outward, make its round, soft edge.
small-circles.result: A round disk with a soft edge.
small-circles.then: Smooth the edge with the same circular motion, so it melts into the gold glow.

mistakes.mistake: The sun's edge is too hard.
mistakes.fix: Soften it with lighter passes. Smudging with a finger works too.

diagram.title: Little circles out from the center

dry-brush.motion: Light pressure, skimming the surface, pulling straight down each trunk.
dry-brush.result: Feathery, broken, see-through gray trunks that catch the canvas texture. Never a solid post.
dry-brush.then: Build the trunks up in several light passes if they're too faint.

mistakes.fix: Let it dry, then dry-brush the background gold or gray back over part of it.

diagram.title: Skim the trunks, with almost no paint

stages.caption: Light, broken strokes down each trunk

dabbing.motion: Tap with the tip of the brush over each leaf clump. The more you tap one spot, the more solid it gets.
dabbing.result: Soft dappled clumps of rust-orange that get more solid the more you tap.
dabbing.then: Leave gaps of the misty gray between the clumps so they stay soft and far away.

mistakes.why: The brush is too wet or holds too much paint.
mistakes.fix: Wipe most of the paint off on a paper towel and tap again.
Let it dry and tap a little of the gray back over it to break it up.

stages.caption: More taps where the clump is thickest

thick-to-thin.motion: Press the full width of the brush for the thick base at the lower left, then turn onto its edge and lighten the pressure as you pull out toward the tips.
thick-to-thin.result: A branch that starts wide at the base and tapers to thin twig tips.
thick-to-thin.then: Add the thinnest twig tips and leaf stems with the tip of the brush.

diagram.title: Wide at the base, then onto the edge

stages.caption: Press the full width at the base
Turn to the edge along the branch

build-from-pieces.motion: Start with one simple shape: a narrow oval along the leaf's middle. Then add the pointed lobes in curved pieces on each side, smaller toward the tip.
build-from-pieces.result: A maple leaf made of distinct pointed pieces, with small gaps or overlaps between them.
build-from-pieces.then: Leave the pieces showing; a few ragged edges look like a real leaf.

stages.caption: A narrow oval down the middle
A lobe on each side, tucked behind

curved-strokes.motion: Bend every stroke with the leaf: from the stem out along each lobe toward its point.
curved-strokes.result: Gold marks that bend with each leaf, which is what makes it look curled and lit.
curved-strokes.then: Keep the gold on the side facing the sun and the orange or red along the shaded side, both following the leaf.

stages.caption: Curved gold strokes on the lit side

flicking.motion: A quick stroke out from inside the body, lifting off as it goes, so each mark thins at its end. On this bird, flick down and back from the head, the way the feathers lie.
flicking.result: Tapered feather marks with broken tips, thickest where the chest faces the sun.
flicking.then: Flick the pale buff over the gold, fewer toward the belly, so the gold shows between the marks.

stages.caption: Fewer, pale buff flicks on top

liner.motion: Hold the brush upright, with light, steady pressure. Pull each leg down from the belly, then curl short toes over the branch, and wobble the edges a little.
liner.result: Thin dark legs and toes gripping the branch.
liner.then: Reload often, a little for each leg.

mistakes.mistake: The toes spread or feather into the branch.
mistakes.why: The branch paint underneath is still wet.
mistakes.fix: Only paint the legs over a dry branch.

steps.tip: The light comes from the upper right, so lay the Leg gray on the side of each leg and toe that faces the light, where the after picture has it. Use a few short, thin lines over the Soft black on each of the two legs, and leave the Soft black showing beneath and between them so the toes still read as dark and sharp.
